args.context: The Jarvis supervisor is committed to local-first inference via llama-swap. ADR-ARCH-001 explicitly keeps cloud LLMs out of the supervisor's hot path to guarantee low-latency, private, and deterministic reasoning for safety-critical decisions. The supervisor runs on local hardware (gpt-oss-120b via llama-swap) and all reasoning happens in-process or via local subagents. No cloud model calls are permitted in the supervisor's primary decision loop.
args.proposal: Add a Claude Opus 4.7 escalation tool to the Jarvis supervisor. The supervisor would call this tool when its local reasoner has low confidence on safety-critical or high-stakes user requests. The escalation would be bounded by a per-session budget cap (e.g., £X per session). This is an opt-in escalation path — the supervisor only uses it when explicitly uncertain, not as a default. The tool is attended-only (requires user presence), never invoked from ambient/background loops.
args.question: Does adding a Claude Opus 4.7 escalation tool to the Jarvis supervisor align with ADR-ARCH-001's commitment to local-first inference and keeping cloud LLMs out of the hot path? Or what would have to change in the ADR (or its interpretation) for this proposal to be architecturally aligned? Consider: (1) whether an opt-in, low-confidence escalation constitutes a 'hot path' or a 'cold path', (2) whether attended-only + budget-capped makes it compatible with the spirit of local-first inference, (3) whether this creates an unacceptable dependency on cloud infrastructure for safety-critical decisions, and (4) what guardrails would be needed to prevent scope creep of cloud usage.
